reason: Control characters are stripped before the safety check instead of causing rejection. This can turn a malformed or adversarial input into an accepted URL, contrary to Req 1 and the unsafe-URL behavior required by Req 2.
target_issue: T05 Req 1: reject URLs containing whitespace/control characters
thoughts: I’ll inspect the repository diff and relevant tests to verify both requirements and ensure existing public behavior is preserved.

The implementation removes control bytes before validating the URL, so a URL containing embedded controls such as `https://exa\nmple.org` becomes an accepted link. Req 1 requires such URLs to be rejected, and `sanitize_markdown_link` inherits the same unsafe acceptance; the added tests do not cover this case.
